name: Soliton Web
desc: The KP-II soliton web computed from its exact tau function — solitary shallow-water waves that ride as straight luminous crests, meet at resonant Y- and X-junctions, cross straight through one another and emerge intact with nothing but a phase shift, the whole web of ridges and tinted plane-wave cells continuously rearranging as the phases drift; a sunlit lagoon with foam crests, a flat-celled tropical curve, tau-potential interference fringes, ironbow thermal, or sumi brush on paper.

energy.doc: brightness + gain of the soliton crests and the cell tints

scale.doc: zoom of the world window — magnifies the web toward a few colossal crests

speed.doc: rate the phases drift and the junctions migrate (0.2 still moves)

density.doc: number of phases, 4 to 8 — sets how many line solitons and junctions weave the web

spread.doc: spread of the k-ladder: sets soliton amplitude ((ki-kj)^2/2) and how steeply the crests lean

cells.doc: how strongly the asymptotic plane-wave cells between the crests are tinted and shaded

hue.doc: primary hue anchoring the water/cell ramp

x.doc: horizontal pan of the world window

y.doc: vertical pan of the world window

style.doc: aesthetic: sunlit lagoon with foam crests / flat-celled tropical curve with hard black lines / tau-potential fringes / ironbow thermal / sumi brush on paper

seed.doc: deterministic seed for the k-ladder and the Vandermonde row
